rules.sentence: Suspect acute diverticulitis if a person presents with constant abdominal pain, usually severe and localising in the left lower quadrant, with any of the following: fever or sudden change in bowel habit and significant rectal bleeding or passage of mucus from the rectum or tenderness in the left lower quadrant, a palpable abdominal mass or distention on abdominal examination, with a previous history of diverticulosis or diverticulitis.
Be aware that in a minority of people and in people of Asian origin, pain and tenderness may be localised in the right lower quadrant.
Suspect complicated acute diverticulitis and refer for same-day hospital assessment if the person has uncontrolled abdominal pain and any of the features in table 1.
